These exchanges do not define every strand of gender or racial-formation analysis.

identity.people: Six contextual selections add Hall, Scott, Smith, Crenshaw, Takaki and D’Emilio, preserving Du Bois, Beard and Lerner. Roles distinguish comparison and criticism; no person is called founder of the teaching umbrella. Constituent traditions retain independent histories.
identity.works_and_arguments: Takaki supplies a concrete multicultural synthesis; Hall, Scott, Smith, Crenshaw and D’Emilio specify arguments rather than generic recognition. Original works, later editions and bounded readings are distinguished. No empty works in this entry; neighboring Hall selection filled with his specific diaspora essay.
identity.internal_distinctions: Six approaches distinguish recovery/agency, multicultural synthesis, experience/exclusion, diaspora, sexual categories/politics and research authority. These are editorial teaching questions, not new schools or mutually exclusive identities.
identity.incoming_connections: All eleven previous neighboring relationships inspected. Fanon’s explicit reception in Hall supplies a specific new contribution. Gender/experience and Indigenous critiques gain bounded primary support; Black, women, social and cultural-studies comparisons now name their limits. Oral, memory, Gilroy and Beard links retain previous qualifications.
identity.outgoing_connections: No outgoing influence is invented for a retrospective teaching umbrella. Its conceptual work is expressed through comparisons and internal distinctions; constituent fields have their own outgoing relationships.
